$comment: Canonical screen/navigation map. Built from iOS's Support/AppRoute.swift + ContentView.swift, Android's ui/ProsaryApp.kt NavHost, and Windows's Navigation/Router.cs usage across Views/*.xaml.cs. Parameter names/types here are the logical contract every platform's own route/query-param/navigation-parameter mechanism should carry, not literal syntax. Keep in sync whenever a screen or its parameters change on any platform — see README.md in this directory.

home.purpose: The Pray tab: a Today section that always shows the weekday and numbered week of the liturgical season, with an English/Hebrew display toggle; optional independently-switchable rows show the chosen calendar's feast and the Pope's monthly intention. The readings row loads that same selected calendar's lectionary table, shows shorthand citations, and can expand them to full citations; a missing date never falls back across rites. Hebrew mode uses sourced title/citation localizations when present and makes the whole Today text stack RTL. Below it is one card per pinned devotion in the user's HomeOrder. The base directory is Rosary, every discovered generic bundle in pack-load order, then Jesus Prayer; saved configurations imply a pin on migration, while FavoriteDevotions lets a user pin/unpin without deleting any saved Prayer. The Rosary card opens its presets surface; generic and Jesus Prayer cards launch the saved default or an unsaved flow/setup when none exists. A fixed Basic Prayers row sits below the cards. Toolbar actions add Rosary/Jesus configurations, restore unpinned devotions, edit order, and open Settings/About where the platform exposes them in-app.

favoriteEditor.purpose: Create or edit a named Rosary or Jesus Prayer configuration: name, default flag, prayer language (including the separate Hebrew Vicariate and Mission choices), kind-specific options, and reminders. An explicitly-Aramaic Rosary also offers its own Sign of the Cross form only when the app default is not Aramaic. Generic bundle devotions use remindersOnlyEditor instead.

prayerId.description: Editing an existing saved configuration. Null when creating new.

newFavoriteKind.description: Seeds a brand-new saved configuration's kind when prayerId is null. iOS passes the whole ad-hoc Prayer object directly instead (sheet(item:)); Android/Windows thread this + prayerId as separate params since neither has an iOS-sheet-style whole-object-across-navigation mechanism.

remindersOnlyEditor.purpose: Compact editor reached from a saved devotion's Pray/preset actions. For generic bundles it renders schema-driven options from options.json followed by reminder times and any manifest reminder presets; for Rosary or Jesus Prayer entries it provides the shared reminders section without reopening the full configuration editor.

prayerId.description: Existing saved Prayer whose options/reminders are edited; this screen never creates a row.

rosaryFlow.purpose: The Rosary prayer flow — season bar, progress, bead track, mystery image/text, Back/Next footer, previous/next-mystery jump controls, and an in-prayer language menu that keeps the same mystery/bead. An unfinished run offers Continue or Restart when this same preset is reopened on the same local day; continuing restores both position and language.

prayerId.description: Saved configuration to pray; null falls back to the default Rosary configuration.

reachedVia.iOS: The generic prayer(id) route -> PrayerDispatchView resolves the Prayer and picks the flow by kind.
reachedVia.android: The generic prayer/{id} route -> PrayerDispatchScreen, same dispatch-by-kind pattern.
reachedVia.windows: Routed to directly by name (RosaryPrayerPage) — the calling Pray/preset surface already holds the full Prayer in memory, so Windows skips the generic-dispatcher indirection used by iOS/Android.

customDevotionFlow.purpose: The single flow for every generic (bundle-driven) devotion (PrayerKind.custom), including Angelus, Stations of the Cross, Via Lucis, Franciscan Crown, Seven Sorrows, Divine Mercy Chaplet, Trisagion, and the O Antiphons. Steps/title/season color are entirely data-driven from devotion.json/manifest.json. Rosary-type bundles render the shared bead track; steps-type bundles use a plain progress bar; days-type bundles add a day menu and tracked progression. The flow can pin/unpin the devotion, choose language and alternate form, edit schema-driven options through the saved row, and show an audio transport when audio.json has a matching language/form track. Chapter hints drive step syncing, manual Back/Next re-aligns audio, and auto-advance stands down during playback. An unfinished run offers Continue or Restart and restores its saved position/language; completion clears it. Adding a generic devotion needs no new screen, only a bundle.

devotionId.description: The bundle id (e.g. "angelus") to load — always required, even when a saved configuration exists, since PrayerKind.custom alone doesn't say which devotion to load.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved configuration. Null when launched from Pray/Categories/Search with no saved row for this devotionId; the flow then uses the app language and bundle defaults. Saved generic rows may carry language, variant, custom options, day progress, and reminders.

reachedVia.iOS: The generic prayer(id) route -> PrayerDispatchView resolves the Prayer and picks CustomDevotionFlowView by kind (reading devotionId from Prayer.customDevotionId); a fresh launch without a saved configuration uses AppRoute.custom(devotionId:) instead.
reachedVia.android: The generic prayer/{id} route -> PrayerDispatchScreen, same dispatch-by-kind pattern; a fresh launch uses the custom/{devotionId} route.
reachedVia.windows: Routed to directly by name (CustomDevotionFlowPage) via CustomDevotionFlowParams(prayerId, bundleId) — Pray/Categories/Search already know the bundle id at the call site, so Windows skips the generic-dispatcher indirection, same as rosaryFlow.

sources.note: Windows' page carries its own copy of RosaryPrayerPage's bead-track XAML (Visibility-bound to ShowsBeadTrack), absorbed from the deleted FranciscanCrownFlowPage — that platform has no shared bead-track control.

jesusPrayerSetup.purpose: Repetition-count picker (33/66/99/Custom/Unbounded) before starting a fresh Jesus Prayer session.

jesusPrayerFlow.purpose: The Jesus Prayer flow — one fixed prayer line plus a repetition counter, with no PrayerEngine step sequence. A star action saves/removes the matching target-and-language configuration so an unsaved setup can be pinned to Pray. A partially counted run offers Continue or Restart on re-entry and clears its bookmark when finished.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved configuration — its own target overrides target, and its language is used.

target.description: Set when launched fresh from jesusPrayerSetup (no saved configuration yet).

jesusPrayerFlow.navigationNote: Finish (pop-to-Home) and the back arrow (pop-one-level, back to Setup) are deliberately distinct commands — see ARCHITECTURE.md and JesusPrayerViewModel's class doc.

about.purpose: Attribution: typefaces, mystery/other image sources, Scripture sources. Static content.

sources.iOS: Views/About/AboutView.swift (Mac: app-menu-only, own window; iPhone/iPad: linked from Pray)

settings.purpose: App-wide preferences: default prayer language (with the Hebrew Vicariate and Mission always listed separately), language fallback precedence edited with the same drag/reorder and reset interaction as Home Order, the system-wide Aramaic Sign of the Cross form, Syriac/Hebrew prayer and Scripture typefaces, auto-advance, phone haptics (iOS/Android), favorite-basic-prayers-first, Pray ordering reset, independent Today-row switches and a feast/reading calendar selection, installed-bundle import/export/removal where supported, audio-cache cleanup, and links to the repository, composer, and privacy policy.

sources.iOS: Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift (macOS Settings scene, Cmd+,; iPhone/iPad sheet from Pray)

rosaryPresetPicker.purpose: Pray -> Rosary: the default preset (one tap to pray), a full Pray-any-Rosary quick setup seeded from it with save-as-preset (never stealing the default slot unless it is the first), then the remaining presets. This surface now owns preset management through each card's edit/reminders/default/delete actions; opening an iPhone context menu must retain the pressed card's visible bounding background. Ad-hoc sessions are unsaved: iOS routes a Prayer value (AppRoute.rosaryQuickPray), Android uses a holder object because Compose routes are strings, and Windows passes the Prayer as the navigation parameter.

repositoryBrowser.purpose: The in-app browser for prayers.prosary.app: fetches the versioned /index.json catalog, filters by search text and tag, and installs through the same installPack pipeline as manual file import. Installed repository bundles gain the manifest-derived 'Repository' tag, appear in Categories/Search, and can be pinned to Pray. Downloads go through the catalog's same-origin /api/download/<id> path so server-side counting works.
repositoryBrowser.navigation: The Browse tab is the primary surface; Search also queries and installs from the same catalog. Manual bundle import lives in Browse/File commands on Apple and Settings on Android/Windows; installed-download management is platform-appropriate Settings UI.

sources.android: ui/favorites/RepositoryBrowserScreen.kt + content/repository/RepositoryClient.kt (the app's only INTERNET-permission feature)

tabShell.purpose: The app's top-level navigation: four sections — Pray, Browse (the prayers.prosary.app catalog), Categories (devotions grouped by manifest tags), and Search (local + community). Phones use a bottom bar; desktop/tablet layouts use a sidebar or rail (iOS 18/macOS 15 sidebarAdaptable, Android NavigationRail at >=840dp, WinUI NavigationView). Active prayer flows hide the bottom bar on iPhone and Android phones, while large-screen sidebars remain. Each iOS tab owns a NavigationStack; Windows resets the frame back stack on section switch so sections behave like tabs.

categories.purpose: View prayers by category: every launchable devotion (Rosary, loaded bundles, Jesus Prayer) grouped by its manifest tags via the shared DevotionDirectory; a devotion appears under each of its tags, untagged ones under 'Other'.

search.purpose: One search across everything prayable: local devotions (opened in place, title/tag match) and the prayers.prosary.app catalog (installed in place); the repository half degrades silently offline.

basicPrayers.purpose: The basic prayers on their own, outside any devotion: Sign of the Cross, Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be, the Creed (the shared tables' Apostles', which the Mission of St. Gamaliel's overlay replaces with the Nicene), and the Trisagion's Holy God — a fixed BasicPrayerCatalog naming keys, never text, so each row and prayer resolves through the same language and fallback chains as the flows. Rows are selectable for copying, reorderable through BasicPrayersOrder, and individually favoritable; favoriteBasicPrayersFirst optionally groups starred prayers at the top without discarding the user's order. Reached from a fixed, non-pinnable row below the Pray cards. Each prayer opens as a single bounded step in the shared flow chrome with Finish as its only action.

parameters.prayerId: BasicPrayerCatalog id ("hailMary") — the single-prayer flow only.
